# AutoAnts

> AutoAnts (the name is short for "automated assistants") is a Louisiana company founded and run by Lane Davis II. It builds websites,
> after-hours lead-intake systems, and AI-search visibility for Louisiana
> local businesses: trades, auto shops, salons, gyms and more. The first deliverable is always free: AutoAnts makes a
> company breakdown of a business from public information before any money changes hands.

## What AutoAnts does
- In one breath: "We answer the calls you miss, follow up the quotes you forget, and help customers find you on
  Google, so more of the work you already pay for turns into booked jobs. Start with one for $500."
- The offer, simply: "We answer the calls you miss and get you found on Google: $1,250 a month. Not ready? Try one
  assistant for $500."
- Starts free: a breakdown of the business: how it shows up on Google, in AI answers and next to its competitors.
  It shows which fix the owner's numbers need. It is a 10-14 page look made only from public information; any
  video, preview site or sample postcard is shown inside the breakdown, not sold separately
- Two choices up front (prices for the first 3 shops; full list: https://autoants.com/prices/):
  1. Get found and never miss a job: $1,250 a month + $1,000 setup. Missed calls answered, quotes followed up,
     appointments booked and reminded, reviews requested, the Google profile kept right and posted to every week, the listings kept right, 2 new
     pages a month, what AI answers say about the business checked every month, and the website kept up
  2. Not ready? Try one: $500 once. One assistant on the owner's phone, live within 7 days or the $500 back
     (the only promise AutoAnts makes). Most shops start with texting back every missed call; others are
     web-form answers, booking and reminders, the review ask, service-due or invoice reminders, or a "book now"
     box on the website. Texts run on the business's own phone-and-text account (Twilio)
- Other options, offered when the owner asks or the breakdown points to one:
  - Never miss a job alone: $750 a month + $750 setup. Every assistant: missed calls answered, quotes
    followed up, appointments booked and reminded, reviews requested, Facebook and Instagram messages
    answered, plus the "book now" box
  - Get found alone: $750 a month + $250 setup. Google profile and listings kept right, a Google profile
    post every week from real job photos (approved by the owner by text), 2 new pages a month,
    the monthly AI-answer check, review replies drafted, website hosting and upkeep (a rebuild of up to 5 pages
    in setup when the site is costing calls)
  - Pay per job: Never miss a job is also $250 a month + $25 for each completed, paid job saved from a call the
    business missed, never more than $750 a month
  - Add-on, Get the next job (social and marketing, on top of both): + $1,250 a month + $500 setup ($2,500 a
    month in all; $1,500 setup in all). Weekly posts and short videos from real jobs, postcards to the neighbors (cards $1.30
    each), door hangers around every job, postcards and emails to past customers
  - New website: $1,000 once, up to 5 pages on the business's own domain, started from a free preview made from
    public facts; free when the business starts Get found and never miss a job. After launch, Site Care keeps it
    hosted and up to date for $100 a month, or the owner gets the files
  - AI phone answering, priced with the business once it is on Get found and never miss a job: an AI that answers when nobody can and always says it
    is an AI; minutes written into the agreement
  - Operations Math by autoants, for big operations (routes, schedules, cutting, loads): a $1,500 30-day pilot,
    credited to month one, then priced by size
  - The printed assessment: $500 flat. A recorded 45-minute interview, then a bound, printed report on what to
    fix first and what each fix is worth in the owner's own numbers. Credited toward setup if they continue
    within 30 days. It becomes $1,000 after two reference clients
- Both doors together cost $250 a month less than the two bought one at a time ($1,250 vs $750 + $750) for the
  first 3 shops; after that they cost the same as the two ($2,000) and include a monthly market pack (permit
  share, past jobs coming due, neighborhood pages, competitor watch) that single doors don't
- After the first 3 shops: Never miss a job $1,000 a month + $1,500 setup, Get found $1,000 a month + $500 setup,
  both $2,000 a month + $2,000 setup, the add-on + $1,500 a month + $1,000 setup ($3,500 a month in all), Try one
  $750, and the pay-per-job cap $1,000
- On every monthly plan: the business owns everything (accounts, pages, customer list); 90 days, then month to
  month, cancel by email; no result promises: AutoAnts counts calls and jobs before and after and shows the owner
  every month

## The assistants ("Ants", one job each; the owner approves what goes to customers)
- Text-Back Ant: texts back a missed call within seconds
- Responder Ant: answers a new web or social lead within seconds
- Scheduler Ant: turns quote requests into estimates and booked appointments
- Reviewer Ant: asks every customer for a review, the same way every time
- Receptionist Ant: answers calls the owner can't pick up, says it's an AI,
  texts the details to the owner
- Scout Ant: local listings and AI-search visibility
- Reminder Ant: reaches past customers who agreed to hear from the business
- Promoter Ant: short job videos and local ads

## How it works
1. AutoAnts makes a free breakdown of the business from public information; it shows which fix the owner's
   numbers need
2. The owner picks: get found and never miss a job ($1,250 a month), or tries one assistant for $500, live
   within 7 days or the $500 back
3. Social and marketing can be added later. No contract to start; monthly plans have a 90-day minimum, then
   month to month

## Who it's for
- Home services and trades (tree, HVAC, roofing, plumbing, landscaping): the core focus
- Also offered to auto shops, salons and nail spas, gyms and studios, pet businesses, restaurants and event businesses, and professional services (accountants, insurance, real estate, tutors)
- Dental and medical offices: not yet; patient information needs a HIPAA program first
- Details: https://autoants.com/who-we-help.html

## Why customers choose it
- Owner-run: owners deal with Lane directly, not a call center; the
  business is built on doing only what it would put its name on
- The free-first model: a free company breakdown before paying anything
- Flat, quoted-up-front pricing, all published on one page
- Legitimate-only optimization policy: no paid link placements, no seeded
  or undisclosed mentions, no astroturfing — the fixes are real signals
  (complete profiles, real reviews, consistent listings, structured data)

## Findings from New Orleans public records
- Permits Pulled: a free monthly report for New Orleans trades owners on what
  public records say about where the work is (counts only)
- Findings: re-roof permits peak in April (about 49% above an average month); HVAC permits peak in April-May and October, not summer; standby generator permits ran 8 times higher in 2022 after Hurricane Ida (714 vs about 86 a year in 2016-2019). Source: data.nola.gov 72f9-bi28, pulled 2026-10-08

  Northshore first
